entries.description:
A key bound to a value, and both of them are runtime VALUES. A key can be a string, a number, a date, a reference to an item -- whatever the language's `=` tells apart, a Map tells apart, so "fr" and "FR" are two keys and 1 is not "1".

A string key is also read after a dot, as it was written: `c.Name` reaches the key "Name", and `c.name` does not. A key is reached by `c[key]`, which raises when nothing is bound to it; by Get, which answers Undefined instead; by Property; and by walking the container, which hands out a KeyValue per entry in the order the keys were inserted.

For a fixed set of NAMES read after a dot in any case, the type is Structure.
How many keys the container holds.
The value bound to the key, or Undefined when nothing is bound to it. It does not raise, which `c[key]` does, and it asks for no second argument, which Property does.
entries.parameters: key — any value. Two string keys are the same key when they are the same text; a key of any other kind is settled by the value's own ordering, and that ordering puts Undefined and Null in one place.
entries.return_descr: The value bound to the key, or Undefined.

entries.description: Whether the key is in the container. What it is bound to is handed back through the second argument, which is left as it was when the key is not there.
entries.parameters:
key — any value.
valueFound — the variable the value is handed back in.
entries.return_descr: Boolean — True when the key is there.

entries.description: Binds a value to a key that is not in the container yet. A key that is already there raises "Key '<key>' is already using!" -- to replace what a key is bound to, assign it: `Rates["fr"] = 2`.
entries.parameters:
key — any value.
value — what to bind to it.

entries.description: Removes the key and what it was bound to. A key that is not there is not an error. The keys that were inserted after it keep their order.
entries.parameters: key — any value. Two string keys are the same key when they are the same text; a key of any other kind is settled by the value's own ordering, and that ordering puts Undefined and Null in one place.

entries.description: Removes every key.

A set of named fields. A field name is a NAME: case does not matter -- `s.Name`, `s.name` and `s["nAmE"]` are one field -- and a field is read after a dot. Only a string can be a field name; anything else is refused.

The fields can be declared when the structure is made, `New Structure("Item, Amount", "Paper", 12)`, or added one at a time with Insert. Walking a structure hands out a KeyValue per field, in the order the fields were added.

When the keys are VALUES rather than names -- a reference, a number, two strings that differ in case -- the type is Map.
entries.parameters:
fields — String, the field names separated by commas. May be left out.
value1, value2, ... — the value of each field in the same order; a field with no value given is Undefined.
entries.return_descr: Structure — with the fields that were declared.

entries.description: How many fields the structure holds.

The value of the field, in any case, or Undefined when the structure has no such field. It does not raise, which `s.Name` and `s["Name"]` do. A name that is not a string is refused, as it is at every other door of a Structure.
entries.parameters: name — String, the field name. Case does not matter.
entries.return_descr: The value of the field, or Undefined.

entries.description: Whether the structure has the field, in any case. Its value is handed back through the second argument, which is left as it was when there is no such field.
entries.parameters:
name — String, the field name.
valueFound — the variable the value is handed back in.
entries.return_descr: Boolean — True when the field is there.

entries.description: Adds a field and gives it a value. The name must be a string and must not be a field already, in any case: a second Insert of "OTHER" after "Other" raises. To change a field, assign it: `s.Other = 2`.
entries.parameters:
name — String, the field name.
value — its value.

entries.description: Removes the field and its value. A name that is not a field is not an error; a name that is not a string is refused.
entries.parameters: name — String, the field name. Case does not matter.

entries.description: Removes every field.
One entry of a Map or a Structure, as walking it hands the entry over: the key and what is bound to it. It is not made with New -- a Foreach over a container or a structure is where it comes from.
The key of the entry: a value in a Map, a field name in a Structure.
What the key is bound to.

A list of values. Add(value, presentation, check, picture) appends an item and returns it; Insert, Get, Count and Clear use an index from zero. Delete takes an item of this list or an index, and refuses anything else. FindByValue returns the item or Undefined. UnloadValues copies the values into a new Array. LoadValues replaces the list with an array of values, unchecked. Copy makes a new list with new items. SortByValue and SortByPresentation sort in place, ascending unless false is passed (as a value table's Sort), and keep equal items in their order. An item given no presentation takes its value's text as one. FillChecks sets every item's check. Move(item, offset) moves an item, or the item at an index, by offset places. list[index] is the item there, and Index(item) is its position, or -1 for an item of another list. Each item has Value (of any type), Presentation, Check and Picture. On a form it is a table that shows the value; the presentation, check and picture can be added. Foreach yields the item. For a query IN, pass list.UnloadValues().

entries.signature: Add(value : any, presentation : string = "", check : boolean = False, picture : StoragePicture = Undefined)
entries.description: Appends an item at the end and answers with it. An item given no presentation takes its value's text as one, at that moment — the form shows it and SortByPresentation sorts by it. The check is False and the picture empty unless they are given.
entries.parameters:
value — what the item holds, any value.
presentation — the text a person sees; left out or empty, the value's text.
check — the item's mark; False when left out.
picture — a picture shown beside the item; left out, none.

entries.signature: Insert(index : number, value : any, presentation : string = "", check : boolean = False, picture : StoragePicture = Undefined)
entries.description: Puts a new item at the index and answers with it; the item that stood there and those after it move down by one. An index equal to Count() appends, as Add does; a larger one raises and nothing is inserted. The other arguments are Add's.
entries.syntax_block: Item = List.Insert(index, value, presentation, check, picture);
entries.parameters:
index — the position the item takes, from 0 to Count().
value, presentation, check, picture — as for Add.
entries.example: List.Insert(0, Undefined, "(none)");   // first in the list

entries.description: How many items the list holds; an empty list answers 0.
The item at the index, counted from 0 — the same as `List[index]`. The item is the list's own, not a copy. An index past the last item raises.

Removes an item — given as the item itself or by its index; the items after it move up by one. An item of another list raises, and so does an index past the last item. Anything that is neither an item nor a number raises too: a string or Undefined is not read as index 0.
entries.parameters: item — an item of this list, or its index from 0.

entries.description: Removes every item; Count() is then 0.
The first item, in list order, whose value equals the given one — or Undefined when there is none. The comparison is strict about type: the number 1 does not find the string "1".
entries.parameters: value — what the item's value must equal.
entries.example: Item = List.FindByValue(2);   // Undefined when no item holds 2

entries.description: The items' values, in list order, as a new Array — without presentations, checks or pictures. It is the form a query parameter for IN takes.

Replaces the whole list with the array's values, one item each, in order: every item's presentation is its value's text, it is unchecked and has no picture. Anything other than an Array raises, and the list is left as it was.
entries.example:
Codes = New Array(); Codes.Add("A"); Codes.Add("B");
List.LoadValues(Codes);

entries.description: A new list with new items holding the same value, presentation, check and picture. Changing an item of the copy leaves the original as it was. The values themselves are not copied: an object an item holds is the same object in both lists.
entries.example:
Backup = List.Copy();
List.Clear();   // Backup keeps its items

entries.description: Reorders the items by their values, in place — ascending unless False is passed. The items themselves move: the list then IS in that order. Items with equal values keep the order they had.
entries.parameters: ascending — True or left out for ascending, False for descending.

entries.description: Reorders the items by their presentations, in place — ascending unless False is passed. Presentations are text and compare as text: "10" comes before "9". Items with equal presentations keep the order they had.
entries.parameters: ascending — True or left out for ascending, False for descending.
entries.example: List.SortByPresentation();   // alphabetical, as a person reads the list

entries.description: Sets every item's check to the value given: True ticks them all, False clears them all.

entries.signature: Move(item : ValueListItem | index : number, offset : number)
entries.description: Moves an item by `offset` places: a positive offset moves it towards the end, a negative one towards the start. The place it would land on must exist — a move past either end raises and nothing moves. The item is given as itself or by its index, as for Delete.
entries.parameters:
item — an item of this list, or its index from 0.
offset — how many places to move it; negative moves it up.
entries.example: List.Move(List.Count() - 1, -1);   // the last item goes one place up

entries.description: Where the item stands in the list, from 0. An item of another list — or anything that is not an item — answers -1.

An item of a value list: the value it holds and how it is shown — Value, Presentation, Check and Picture. It is the list's OWN item, not a copy: writing a property changes the list, and the same item reached twice — by index, by FindByValue, by Foreach — is the same item. Items are made by the list's Add and Insert, never with New.
What the item holds — any value, read and written. The presentation an item took from its value when it was added stays as it was when the value is written later.

The text a person sees for the item, and what SortByPresentation sorts by. Whatever is written is kept as its text: `Item.Presentation = 12` holds "12". An item whose presentation is empty is shown by its value's text.
The item's mark, True or False — a list shown with check boxes reads and writes it. A value written is kept as a Boolean.
A picture shown beside the item. An item added without one holds an empty picture (a StoragePicture with nothing in it), never Undefined.
